p.i: Samuel the Lamanite’s prophecy to the Nephites.

chapter.li: LEChapter13 Verse1 In the 86th year, the Nephites remained unrepentant, indeed, persistently wicked, while the Lamanites were careful to strictly keep God’s commandments according to the Law of Moses. VerseEnd Verse2 In this year a man named Samuel, a Lamanite, came to Zarahemla and began to preach to the people. He preached repentance to the people for many days, but they threw him out, and as he was returning to his own land, VerseEnd Verse3 the Lord’s voice spoke to him, telling him to return and prophesy to the people everything that would enter his heart. VerseEnd

Verse4 But they wouldn’t let him reenter the city. Therefore he climbed atop the city wall and reached out his arm and shouted in a loud voice, prophesying to the people everything the Lord put into his heart. VerseEnd Verse5 He declared to them: I’m Samuel, a Lamanite, and I’m telling 2PP you the words the Lord puts into my heart. He has this message for this people: The sword of justice hangs over 2PP you. And before 400 years have passed, the sword of justice will fall upon 2PP you. VerseEnd Verse6 Indeed, terrible destruction awaits 2PP you. It will certainly come for 2PP you, and nothing can save 2PP you except repentance and faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. He is assuredly coming into the world to suffer many things and be killed on behalf of His people. VerseEnd Verse7 An angel of the Lord testified of this to me; he’s brought me this good news. I was sent to testify of it to 2PP you as well, so 2PP you also hear this good news. But 2PP you refused to listen to me. VerseEnd

Verse8 Therefore the Lord now says: Because of the hardness of the hearts of the Nephites, unless they repent, I’ll take away My salvation from them and I’ll withdraw My Spirit from them. I won’t put up with them any longer, and I’ll let the hearts of their Lamanite brothers and sisters turn against them. VerseEnd Verse9 And before 400 years have passed, I’ll bring afflictions, punishing them with the sword, famine, and with disease; VerseEnd Verse10 indeed, they’ll bring down My fury. And there will be those of the fourth generation of 2PP your enemies, who will live to see 2PP your complete destruction. The Lord warns: This is certain to happen unless 2PP you repent to avoid the fourth generation seeing 2PP your destruction. VerseEnd Verse11 But the Lord says: If 2PP you repent and return to the Lord 2PP your God, I’ll turn My anger away. Indeed, the Lord says: Blessed are those who repent and turn to Me, but woe upon those who don’t repent. VerseEnd Verse12 Woe to this great city of Zarahemla! It’s only because of the righteous that it’s saved. Woe to this great city! The Lord says: I see that many, indeed, the majority of the inhabitants of this great city, have chosen to harden their hearts against Me. VerseEnd Verse13 But blessed are those who repent, since I’ll spare them. If it weren’t for the few righteous in this great city, I would send fire down from heaven and destroy it. VerseEnd Verse14 But it’s spared because of the righteous. The Lord says: The time will come, once 2PP you drive away the righteous, 2PP you will be ripe for destruction.

Woe to this great city because of the wickedness and abominations that are in her. VerseEnd Verse15 Woe to the city of Gideon because of the wickedness and abominations in her. VerseEnd Verse16 Woe to all the cities, in every direction, inhabited by the Nephites, because of the wickedness and abominations in them. VerseEnd Verse17 A curse will fall on the land, says the Lord of Hosts, because of the wickedness and abominations of the people living there. VerseEnd

Verse18 And it will happen, says the Lord of Hosts (our great and true God), that any who protect their wealth by hiding it in the ground will never recover it because the land will be cursed. Only the righteous will be able to protect what’s stored for the Lord’s sake. VerseEnd Verse19 The Lord says: I want them to protect their valuable possessions for My purposes. But everyone who doesn’t safeguard their wealth for My sake is cursed, because only the righteous protect their valuable things for My sake. Any others who hoard their wealth are cursed, both them and their wealth, for it will be lost because of the curse upon the land. VerseEnd Verse20 The day is coming when they’ll hoard wealth because they’ve set their hearts on their property. Because they’ve set their hearts on their property and will hide it away when they flee from their enemies, they and their property will be cursed, and everything and everyone will be lost on that day, says the Lord. VerseEnd

Verse21 People of this great city, listen to me. Listen to the words of the Lord. He says 2PP your wealth has become a curse to 2PP you; 2PP you and 2PP your wealth are both cursed because that’s all 2PP you value, and 2PP you won’t listen to the words of the One who gave it to 2PP you. VerseEnd Verse22 2PP You’ve forgotten the Lord who is God because of what He’s blessed 2PP you with. However, 2PP you always remember 2PP your property, never thanking the Lord 2PP your God for it. 2PP Your hearts never focus on the Lord; instead, 2PP you’re full of great pride leading to bragging and awful arrogance, to jealousy, conflicts, malice, persecutions, murders, and all kinds of iniquities. VerseEnd Verse23 For this reason, the Lord God has cursed the land and 2PP your property also — and this is because of 2PP your iniquities. VerseEnd Verse24 Woe to this people because 2PP you now drive out the prophets, ridicule them, throw stones at them, kill them, and abuse them, just like they’ve done before. VerseEnd

Verse25 When 2PP you mention it, 2PP you claim: If we had lived during the time of our ancestors long ago, we wouldn’t have killed the prophets; we wouldn’t have stoned them and driven them out. VerseEnd Verse26 But 2PP you’re worse than them. Because as the Lord lives, if a prophet comes to 2PP you and declares the Lord’s word, telling of 2PP your sins and iniquities, 2PP you’re enraged at him and throw him out and look for a way to kill him. Indeed, 2PP you’ll claim he’s a false prophet, a sinner, and follows the accuser because he testifies about 2PP your evils. VerseEnd Verse27 But if a man tells 2PP you: Do this; it isn’t iniquity! Do that; 2PP you won’t suffer for it! Indeed, if he says: Live 2PP your life proudly; never be ashamed of what others see 2PP you doing, and do as 2PP you please. When someone is teaching this, 2PP you want to hear it. 2PP You’ll say he’s a prophet; VerseEnd Verse28 2PP you’ll support him. 2PP You’ll give him some of 2PP your wealth and pay him with 2PP your gold and silver; 2PP you’ll clothe him with expensive clothing. And because he assures 2PP you and says everything is fine, 2PP you won’t find any fault with him. VerseEnd

Verse29 2PP You wicked and perverse generation, 2PP you hardened and stubborn people, how long do 2PP you think the Lord will put up with 2PP you? How long will 2PP you allow yourselves to be led by foolish and blind guides? How long will 2PP you choose darkness rather than light? VerseEnd Verse30 The Lord’s anger is already aroused against 2PP you. He’s cursed the land because of 2PP your iniquity. VerseEnd Verse31 The time is coming when He’ll curse 2PP your wealth; it will slip away and 2PP you won’t be able to hold onto it; and when poverty overtakes 2PP you, 2PP your wealth won’t come back. VerseEnd Verse32 In the days of 2PP your poverty 2PP you’ll appeal to the Lord, but that won’t help; because desolation will have arrived, and 2PP your destruction is certain. 2PP You’ll weep and howl on that day, says the Lord of Hosts. Then 2PP you’ll lament and say: VerseEnd Verse33 I wish I had repented and hadn’t killed, stoned, and driven out the prophets. Then 2PP you’ll ask: Why didn’t we remember the Lord our God at the time He blessed us with abundance? Then our wealth wouldn’t have slipped away and been lost, and now we suffer poverty. VerseEnd Verse34 We put a tool here, and the next day it disappears. We can’t find our swords in the day of battle as we search for them. VerseEnd Verse35 We’ve stored our valuable things, and they’ve slipped away from us because of the curse on the land. VerseEnd Verse36 Why didn’t we repent when the Lord’s word came to us? The land is cursed; everything is unstable, and we can’t hold onto anything. VerseEnd Verse37 We’re surrounded by demons, surrounded by the angels of him who attempts to destroy our souls. Indeed, we’ve sinned terribly. O Lord, we beg 2PSI You to turn 2PSI Your anger away from us! This will be 2PP your plea in those days. VerseEnd

Verse38 But the days of 2PP your probation have ended. 2PP You’ve procrastinated the day of 2PP your salvation until it’s everlastingly too late and 2PP your destruction is now certain. 2PP You’ve tried 2PP your whole lives to get what’s impossible: 2PP You’ve tried to find happiness in committing iniquity, which violates the nature of the righteousness of our great and eternal Head. VerseEnd Verse39 People of this land, I wish 2PP you would listen to me! I pray the Lord’s anger can still be turned away from 2PP you, and ask 2PP you to repent and be saved. VerseEnd

LEChapter14 Verse1 Now Samuel the Lamanite prophesied many more things that can’t be written. VerseEnd Verse2 But he did tell them: I’ll give 2PP you a sign. Five years from now, the Son of God will come to redeem all those who believe in His name. VerseEnd Verse3 I’ll give 2PP you this as a sign of when He comes. There will be great lights in heaven, and in the night before He comes there will be no darkness, so it will seem to people as if it’s still daytime. VerseEnd Verse4 Therefore there will be a day, a night, and a day, as a single daytime without any night. This is a signal to 2PP you, since 2PP you’ll observe the rising and setting of the sun. Therefore it will be obvious there were two days and a night; nevertheless, the night won’t be dark. That will be on the night before He’s born. VerseEnd Verse5 A new star will arise, unlike anything 2PP you’ve seen; and this will be another signal to 2PP you. VerseEnd Verse6 But this isn’t all, because there will be many signals and astonishing things in heaven. VerseEnd Verse7 All of 2PP you will be amazed and astonished, so much so that 2PP you’ll fall to the ground. VerseEnd Verse8 Those who believe in the Son of God will have everlasting life. VerseEnd

Verse9 The Lord has commanded me by His angel to come and tell 2PP you this. He’s commanded me to prophesy these things to 2PP you; He directed me: Proclaim to this people: Repent and prepare to follow the Lord. VerseEnd Verse10 Now, because I’m a Lamanite and told 2PP you the words the Lord commanded me to speak which condemn 2PP you, 2PP you’re angry with me, are trying to kill me, and have driven me away. VerseEnd Verse11 Despite this, 2PP you’re going to hear my words, which is why I’ve climbed atop the walls of this city: so 2PP you would hear and know of God’s judgments awaiting 2PP you because of 2PP your iniquities; so 2PP you could know the offenses requiring 2PP your repentance; VerseEnd Verse12 and so 2PP you know about the coming of Jesus Christ, the Son of God the Father of heaven and of earth, the Creator of all things from the beginning; and so 2PP you are aware of the signs of His coming, so 2PP you can believe in His name. VerseEnd Verse13 If 2PP you believe in His name, 2PP you’ll repent of all 2PP your sins, to receive a remission of 2PP your sins through Him. VerseEnd

Verse14 In addition, I’ll tell 2PP you of another sign coming at His death. VerseEnd Verse15 Because He certainly must die to bring salvation. It’s necessary and proper for Him to die in order to bring about the resurrection of the dead, so that mankind can return to the Lord’s presence. VerseEnd Verse16 His death precedes His resurrection and will redeem everyone from the first death, that spiritual death. Because all mankind was cut off from the Lord’s presence when Adam fell, they’re effectively dead both physically and spiritually. VerseEnd Verse17 But Christ’s resurrection redeems all mankind and returns them to the Lord’s presence. VerseEnd Verse18 And it establishes the conditions for repentance, so whoever repents isn’t cut down and thrown into the fire. But whoever doesn’t repent is cut down and thrown into the fire. Then a second, spiritual death happens to them, because they’re cut off again from all righteousness. VerseEnd Verse19 Therefore repent, repent, or else by knowing these things and failing to do them, 2PP you’ll come under condemnation and bring this second death down upon 2PP you. VerseEnd

Verse20 But as I told 2PP you about another sign, a sign of His death: On the day of His death, the sun will become dark and refuse to give his light to 2PP you, and the moon and stars as well. There won’t be any light on this land for three days, from the time when He suffers death to the time when He rises from the dead. VerseEnd Verse21 When He dies, when He breathes His last, there will be thunder and lightning for many hours. The earth will shake and tremble, and the rock of the earth, both above the ground and beneath it, which 2PP you see is now solid, or most of it is one solid mass, will be fractured apart; VerseEnd Verse22 it will be broken apart into grooves, cracks, and broken fragments from then on, across the whole earth, both above the ground and beneath it. VerseEnd Verse23 And there will be great storms. Many mountains will be laid low like a valley. Many places now called valleys will become very high mountains. VerseEnd Verse24 Many highways will be broken up, and many cities will be decimated. VerseEnd Verse25 And many graves will be opened and will give up many of their dead; with many holy ones seen by many witnesses. VerseEnd Verse26 The angel has told me the following: He said there would be thunder and lightning for many hours. VerseEnd Verse27 He told me that while the thunder and lightning and storm lasted, as this takes place darkness will cover the entire land for three days. VerseEnd Verse28 The angel also told me many would see greater things than these, in order for them to believe — that these signs and these wonders would happen throughout this land, so there wouldn’t be any reason for unbelief by mankind — VerseEnd Verse29 and so that whoever chose to believe could be saved and whoever didn’t believe could have a righteous judgment imposed on them; and so if they’re condemned, they chose their own condemnation. VerseEnd

Verse30 Now remember, remember, my friends, that whoever perishes, perishes by their own choice and whoever does evil does it to themselves. Because 2PP you’re free; 2PP you’re permitted to act for yourselves. God has given 2PP you a choice, and He lets 2PP you freely make it. VerseEnd Verse31 He’s made 2PP you capable of distinguishing good from evil. He lets 2PP you choose life or death. 2PP You can do good and be restored to what’s good or have what’s good restored to 2PP you; or 2PP you can do evil and have what’s evil restored to 2PP you. VerseEnd LEChapter15 Verse1 Now, my dear people, I declare to 2PP you that unless 2PP you repent, 2PP your houses will be left completely abandoned. VerseEnd Verse2 Unless 2PP you repent, 2PP your women will have good reason to mourn when they nurse their young. 2PP You’ll attempt to escape and there won’t be any safe place to go. Woe to those who are pregnant, since pregnancy will slow them down and they won’t be able to escape; they will struggle, fall down, and be left to die. VerseEnd Verse3 Woe to 2PP you people called Nephites, unless 2PP you repent when 2PP you see all the signs and astonishing things that will be shown to 2PP you. Because 2PP you’ve been a chosen people of the Lord. He’s loved the Nephites. And He’s corrected 2PP you as well when 2PP you strayed because He loves 2PP you. VerseEnd

Verse4 But, my friends, He’s detested the Lamanites because they’ve continually done evil — but only because of their ancestors’ wicked traditions. But salvation has come to them through the Nephites’ preaching; and because of this, the Lord will assure their descendants’ survival. VerseEnd Verse5 I tell 2PP you the majority of them are following their duty faithfully, living carefully before God, taking care to keep His commandments, statutes, and judgments according to the Law of Moses. VerseEnd Verse6 I tell 2PP you the majority of them do this. They continue tirelessly to work on converting the rest of their fellow Lamanites to the truth. Therefore many others join them daily. VerseEnd Verse7 2PP You’ve seen and know that all who are converted to the truth, abandon the wicked and perverse traditions of their ancestors, and are persuaded to believe the holy scriptures (the prophecies of the holy prophets written there), which led them to faith in the Lord and to repentance, which faith and repentance bring them a change of heart; VerseEnd Verse8 therefore 2PP you know all of them are firm and resolute in the liberty God has given them. VerseEnd Verse9 2PP You also know they’ve buried their weapons, and they’re afraid to use them because they might sin in some way. 2PP You can see they’re afraid to commit sin. They’ll allow themselves to be cut down and killed by their enemies and won’t resist them. They refuse because of their faith in Christ. VerseEnd

Verse10 Now because once converted to the truth they’re steadfast in their beliefs, and because they’re firm once they accept the truth, the Lord will bless them and preserve their descendants, despite their iniquity. VerseEnd Verse11 Indeed, even if they fall away into unbelief, the Lord will watch over their posterity until the time arrives prophesied by our forefathers, and by the prophet Zenos, and many other prophets as well, about the restoration of the Lamanites to the knowledge of the truth. VerseEnd Verse12 I tell 2PP you that in the last days the Lord’s promises cover the Lamanites, our friends and relatives. Despite coming hardships for them, and despite being driven here and there on the earth, hunted, afflicted, and scattered about, having no place for refuge, still, the Lord is going to be merciful to them. VerseEnd Verse13 This will fulfill the prophecy that they will return to the true knowledge, meaning the knowledge of their Redeemer, their great and true Shepherd, and be included as His sheep. VerseEnd Verse14 Therefore I tell 2PP you: It’s going to be better for them than for 2PP you unless 2PP you repent. VerseEnd Verse15 Because if the powerful miracles had been shown to them that have been shown to 2PP you, 2PP you can see for yourselves they wouldn’t have fallen away in unbelief ever again. No, they only fell away into unbelief because of their ancestors’ traditions. VerseEnd Verse16 Therefore the Lord says: I won’t completely destroy them, but in the day of My wisdom I’ll lead them back to Me, says the Lord. VerseEnd Verse17 Now the Lord says to the Nephites: If 2PP you don’t repent and take care to do My will, I’ll completely destroy 2PP you, says the Lord, because of 2PP your unbelief, despite the many powerful miracles I performed among 2PP you. And as surely as the Lord lives, these things will happen, says the Lord. VerseEnd

LEChapter16 Verse1 Now there were many who heard what Samuel the Lamanite said from the city walls. All those who believed what he said went looking for Nephi. When they found him, they confessed their sins to him and didn’t deny them, asking to be baptized in the name of the Lord. VerseEnd Verse2 But all those who didn’t believe Samuel’s message were angry at him. They threw stones, and many also shot arrows at him as he stood on the wall. But the Spirit of the Lord was with him, so they missed him with their stones or arrows. VerseEnd

Verse3 When they saw they couldn’t hit him, many more believed what he said, so they also went to Nephi to be baptized. VerseEnd Verse4 Nephi was baptizing, prophesying, preaching, crying repentance to the people, showing them signs and awe-inspiring things, and performing miracles among the people, so they would know Christ was sure to come soon. VerseEnd Verse5 He taught them about other things that would happen soon, so that when they happened they would remember they had been revealed to them beforehand, and would believe. Therefore all who believed in Samuel’s words went to Nephi to be baptized, because they came repenting and confessing their sins. VerseEnd

Verse6 But the majority didn’t believe what Samuel said. Therefore when they saw they couldn’t hit him with stones and arrows, they yelled to their captains: Arrest this man and tie him up. He’s possessed by a devil; and because of the power of the accuser protecting him, we can’t hit him with our stones and arrows! So arrest him and tie him up and take him away! VerseEnd Verse7 As they went to lay their hands on him, he jumped down from the wall and escaped from their lands, returning to his own country, where he continued to preach and prophesy among his own people. VerseEnd Verse8 He was never heard from again by the Nephites. And this tells 2PP you the condition of the people. VerseEnd Verse9 So ended the 86th year of the judges’ rule over the Nephites. VerseEnd Verse10 And so ended also the 87th year of the judges’ rule — most of the people remaining prideful and wicked and a minority living carefully before God. VerseEnd Verse11 It was the same in the 88th year of the judges’ rule. VerseEnd Verse12 In the 89th year of the judges’ rule, there was little change in the people’s affairs, except that the people began to be more entrenched in iniquity and increasingly disobedient to God’s commandments. VerseEnd

Verse13 But in the 90th year of the judges’ rule, great signs were given to the people, and other awe-inspiring things as the prophet’s words began to be fulfilled. VerseEnd Verse14 Angels appeared to wise men declaring to them good news of great joy. In this year, the scriptures began to be fulfilled. VerseEnd Verse15 Nevertheless, the people still hardened their hearts, except for the most believing of them, among both the Nephites and the Lamanites. They began to rely on their own reasoning and foolishness, saying: VerseEnd Verse16 They may have guessed right about a few things among so many. But certainly, all the great and miraculous things predicted will never happen. VerseEnd Verse17 They began to reason and argue among themselves, VerseEnd Verse18 saying it wasn’t at all reasonable for any Messiah to come, but if he does come, and he really is the son of God the Father of heaven and of earth, as claimed, then why won’t he show himself to us as well as to those at Jerusalem? VerseEnd Verse19 Why won’t he come to this land as well as to the land of Jerusalem? VerseEnd Verse20 But clearly this is a wicked tradition handed down to us by our ancestors, to make us believe in some great and miraculous thing to happen, but not among us, but in a land that’s far away, a land we know nothing about. Therefore they can keep us in ignorance, since we can’t witness with our own eyes when it happens. VerseEnd Verse21 And using this clever and unseen trick from the Evil One, they’ll make claims we’ll never be able to disprove, which will be used to control us as servants to them and their false tradition, since we depend on them as our teachers. So they’ll keep us in ignorance our whole lives, if we let them. VerseEnd

Verse22 The people imagined many other foolish, vain lies to believe. And they were very agitated, since Satan constantly stirred them up to sin. He went around spreading rumors and starting conflicts everywhere, in order to harden the people’s hearts toward the truth and to reject the prophesies. VerseEnd Verse23 Despite the signs and marvelous things that happened among the Lord’s people and the many miracles they experienced, Satan controlled the people’s hearts throughout the land. VerseEnd Verse24 And so ended the 90th year of the judges’ rule. VerseEnd Verse25 And so ended the Book of Helaman, based on the record of Helaman and his sons. VerseEnd
